title: Divisional Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-I v. Raman Singh & Another
disposition: Writ petition dismissed (Permanent Lok Adalat compensation upheld)
headnote: For a consumer's electricity dispute, the Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 are a comprehensive code, and the jurisdiction of the civil court is expressly barred by Section 145 of the Act. But a claim by a member of the public for damages caused by the licensee's fault — here, livestock electrocuted by a snapped 11 KV line — is not a consumer/Code matter: 'supply of power' is a 'public utility service' under Section 22-A of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, so such a claim falls within the jurisdiction of the Permanent Lok Adalat, and the CGRF/Ombudsman Regulations, 2007 (which cover only consumer grievances) do not apply. Electricity distribution being a hazardous activity, the licensee is under a duty to maintain its lines.

holding_units.code: Electricity Act, 2003 (with Supply Code 2005 & CGRF Regulations 2007)
holding_units.topic: Forum: consumer disputes (Code/civil-court bar) vs a non-consumer's tort claim (Lok Adalat)
holding_units.question: Does the Permanent Lok Adalat have jurisdiction over a non-consumer's claim for damages for electrocution of livestock by the licensee's line, or is it barred by the Electricity Act / Supply Code scheme?
holding_units.holding: For a consumer's dispute, the Act and the Supply Code are comprehensive and civil-court jurisdiction is barred by Section 145. A non-consumer's claim for tort damages against the licensee is not a Code/CGRF matter; 'supply of power' is a 'public utility service' under Section 22-A of the LSA Act, 1987, so the Permanent Lok Adalat has jurisdiction, and the CGRF/Ombudsman Regulations, 2007 (covering only consumer grievances) do not apply. The compensation award is upheld.
holding_units.limiting_facts: An unattended snapped 11 KV line electrocuted the claimant's buffalo (his livelihood); the claimant was not a consumer; the licensee stalled even the admitted compensation for ~3 years on a jurisdiction plea.

principle_tags.application: The Supply Code and its CGRF/Ombudsman forum cover consumer grievances, not a non-consumer's tort-damages claim against the licensee; such claims lie before the Permanent Lok Adalat as a public-utility-service dispute.

lead_authorities.name: Bar Council of India v. Union of India
S.N. Pandey v. Union of India

principle_tags.application: Electricity distribution is a hazardous activity; the licensee is under a statutory duty to maintain its installations and lines so that passers-by (human or animal) are not harmed.

lead_authorities.name: Shakuntala Devi v. Delhi Electric Supply Undertaking

authorities.name: Bar Council of India v. Union of India
authorities.proposition: Permanent Lok Adalats under Chapter VI-A of the LSA Act, 1987 have jurisdiction over disputes concerning public utility services (including supply of power) up to a pecuniary limit, in addition to and not in derogation of other fora, before the dispute is brought to a court.
authorities.how_treated: Relied on to sustain the Permanent Lok Adalat's jurisdiction.

authorities.name: S.N. Pandey v. Union of India
authorities.proposition: Upholds the validity of the Permanent Lok Adalat mechanism for deciding disputes involving public utility services as an alternative dispute-resolution forum.
authorities.how_treated: Relied on in support of the Lok Adalat's adjudicatory jurisdiction.

authorities.name: Smt. Shakuntala Devi v. Delhi Electric Supply Undertaking & Ors.
authorities.proposition: A statutory electricity authority has a duty to maintain its electric installations and lines in proper condition so as to avoid any threat to the lives of people.
authorities.how_treated: Relied on to fix the licensee's duty and negligence.
